exact_statement: For the scalar-integrator, fixed connected undirected graph, global shared-medium DoS, and self-triggered protocol specified by Senejohnny–Tesi–De Persis (2015), their stated condition 1/tau_d + Delta_*/tau_f < 1, with Delta_*=epsilon/(4 d_min), is sufficient for finite-time convergence to the practical-consensus set |ave_i|<epsilon for every node.
assumptions: All nodes and states are fault-free.
DoS disables all communication across one shared medium at once.
Fixed connected undirected graph; exact real-valued relative-state polling at local events.
DoS start-frequency and total-duration envelopes hold for every time interval.
status: source-reported; interface and proof steps internally reconstructed
proof_path: SOURCES.md; sources/Senejohnny_Tesi_DePersis_2015.tex, Section II-A, Section II-B, Section III-A equations (19)-(20), Section III-B proof of Proposition 2 and Theorem 2
novelty_boundary: Established source result as reported by the primary paper; not externally revalidated here. It does not cover independent per-link DoS or Byzantine nodes.
costs: Per sample each node polls all d_i neighbors and computes ave_i; transmission, receive, sensor, trigger-computation, and actuation joules are not priced in the theorem.
falsifier: A counterexample satisfying the paper's global shared-medium model and its stated frequency/duration bounds but not reaching the practical-consensus set would falsify this source claim.
next_gate: Reconstruct full journal proof and distinguish its global channel model from any edge-wise extension.

exact_statement: In a directed K4 with common retry interval delta=Delta_*=epsilon/12, if every receiver loses one incoming edge at each event and the missing edge rotates through its three in-neighbors, with each edge outage of duration rho=delta/10 recurring every 3 delta, then every edge satisfies the scalar PoC expression phi_e=11/30<1 while a fail-closed complete-neighborhood controller receives no complete neighbor vector at any event and remains at any post-transient state whose diameter exceeds epsilon.
assumptions: Four scalar agents, complete directed graph without self-links, synchronous event times.
At each event one incoming edge per receiver is unavailable; edge identities rotate with period three events.
Outage windows cover the event instant and last rho=delta/10.
The specified full-vector controller sets control to zero and retries after delta whenever any input is missing.
The state after the first failed event has diameter greater than epsilon.
status: internally reconstructed counterexample; edge schedules and inequalities exact
novelty_boundary: This refutes only applying the source's global shared-channel PoC inequality separately to each edge for this fail-closed event interface. It does not refute the original theorem or all event-triggered protocols. External novelty is UNKNOWN.
costs: Per event 12 directed transmission attempts, 8 successful receives, 4 drops, 4 local state samples, and 12 link-presence checks. Failed transmissions are charged; hardware joules are UNKNOWN.
falsifier: Show a complete neighbor vector at one of the specified event times, or identify an error in the exact outage envelopes or the stated controller transition.
next_gate: Test whether a failure-aware retry or event-time randomization closes the gap under the same per-edge budget, then add Byzantine nodes with an event-sampled robust-connectivity condition.

exact_statement: For the same K4 event graph sequence, where phase r in {1,2,3} omits sender i+r mod 4 at receiver i, the baseline that averages each node's own state and its two received neighbor values has exact three-event product with minimum row overlap 26/27 and Dobrushin coefficient 1/27; hence diameter after 3m events is at most 27^(-m) times its initial value.
assumptions: Same synchronous events and same eight successfully delivered values per event as RD-02.
No Byzantine nodes; values are scalar and unquantized.
Each node uses equal weights on itself and its two received neighbors.
status: internally reconstructed conditional theorem; exact finite rational computation
novelty_boundary: Exact calculation for one periodic four-node schedule; not a general theorem for arbitrary graphs or adversaries. Novelty/priority UNKNOWN.
costs: Same 12 directed attempts, 8 receives, and 4 local samples per event as RD-02; 8 additions, 4 multiplications by 1/3, and 4 state updates per event.
falsifier: Exact matrix multiplication or an exact row-overlap calculation disagreeing with the stored product or coefficient.
next_gate: Extend the product argument to an event-sampled W-MSR update under a named F-total or F-local model and count sorting, sensing, messaging, and actuation.
